{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=experimental+methods+to+distinguish+between+chemical+memory+and+hysteresis+in+autocatalytic+reaction+networks&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.1021/acs.jctc.5c01979.s001\", \"title\": [\"Enumeration of Autocatalytic Subsystems in Large Chemical Reaction Networks\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.5c01979.s001\"}, {\"DOI\": \"10.21203/rs.3.rs-4379130/v1\", \"title\": [\"Exploring the Programmability of Autocatalytic Chemical Reaction Networks\"], \"abstract\": \"Abstract\\n

Chemical reaction networks (CRNs) could offer chemical complexity1 to contribute to future intelligent material design2 or neuromorphic computing technologies3,4. Recent advances in systems chemistry use the complex Belousov–Zhabotinsky5-7 and Formose reactions8,9, or simpler chemical systems with fewer feedback loops10-12, to demonstrate that (spatio)temporal patterns can be harnessed to emulate properties important for intelligent behavior (i.e., the ability to perceive information and retain it as knowledge to execute complex tasks13). In all examples, autocatalysis appears an essential element for facilitating a nonlinear response. How this chemical analogue of a positive feedback mechanism14,15 can be reconfigured in a programmable manner is, however, unknown. Here, we developed a strategy that uses metal ions (Ca2+, La3+, and Nd3+) to control the rate of a trypsin-catalysed autocatalytic reaction network. A flow setup is employed to sustain the reaction network under out-of-equilibrium conditions and demonstrate that various kinetically controllable responses can be mapped onto polynomial and Boolean functions. Remarkably, these functions cannot only be programmed but their temporal and history-dependent nature bestows them with neuromorphic properties, promising novel strategies in designing intelligent chemical systems. Beyond, the easy-to-use method to control autocatalysis will impact future development focusing on biocatalysis, nanobiotechnology, and the chemical origin of life.

We also provide a linear-programming algorithm to exhaustively enumerate them and a scheme to visualize their polyhedral geometry and combinatorics. We then define cluster chemical reaction networks, a framework for coarse-graining realistic chemical reactions using conservation laws. We find that the list of minimal autocatalytic subnetworks in a maximally connected cluster chemical reaction network with one conservation law grows exponentially in the number of species. review.alternative: Objective states may emerge from intrinsic system properties rather than environmental encoding.
review.would_change_mind: Observations of stable records in isolated quantum systems without decoherence.

claims.statement: The objective character of the macroscopic world arises from quantum-to-classical transitions where system pointer states are redundantly encoded into environmental degrees of freedom.

support.explanation: This establishes the problem of objectivity as a core aspect of quantum-to-classical transition.
support.passage: The problem of objectivity, i.e. how to explain on quantum grounds the objective character of the macroscopic world, is one of the aspects of the celebrated quantum-to-classical transition.

review.alternative: Observer consensus might rely on pre-existing quantum correlations (e.g., entanglement) rather than broadcasted records.
review.would_change_mind: Measurement showing observer consensus persists without the presence of redundant environmental pointers.

claims.statement: Observer consensus is mediated by the environment acting as a broadcast structure, allowing for consistent information retrieval.

support.explanation: This supports the role of an aperture function in managing accessible information for independent observers.
support.passage: The A/R/F framework distinguishes environmental redundancy from the effective redundancy usable by a specific observer, models accessibility through a noisy-threshold aperture function

actions.findings:
The objective character of the macroscopic world arises from quantum-to-classical transitions where system pointer states are redundantly encoded into environmental degrees of freedom. [peer-d062550a82ade2a0aa128e16]

Observer consensus is mediated by the environment acting as a broadcast structure, allowing for consistent information retrieval. [peer-a8016408356a25cdef545dbe]
actions.limitations: Current operational definitions rely on Markovian assumptions for environmental coupling; non-Markovian dynamics and specific high-inertia regimes may challenge these findings.
actions.next_questions: How do non-Markovian interactions alter the temporal stability of the broadcasted record across independent observers?
actions.reason: Revision reflects the integration of the A/R/F framework into our understanding of record accessibility and robustness.
actions.summary: Robust records emerge when quantum systems redundantly encode information into the environment (decoherence), facilitating consistent access for independent observers. This robustness is formally captured by Spectrum Broadcast Structures (SBS) and the A/R/F framework, which distinguishes between environmental redundancy and observer-specific accessible information.
actions.title: Robustness of Physical Records Across Independent Observers

proposal.summary: This research iteration updates the analysis of physical record robustness, focusing on the role of redundant environmental encoding and spectrum broadcast structures in facilitating observer agreement. We assess how decoherence-driven broadcast mechanisms support the emergence of objective records and detail current limitations regarding non-Markovian system dynamics.
proposal.title: Robustness of Physical Records and Observer Consensus
